title: Dynamic Node Creation in Backpropagation Networks
summary: Introduces Dynamic Node Creation, a constructive approach in which a backpropagation network can add hidden units during training instead of fixing hidden-layer size in advance.
growth_mechanism: Adds hidden nodes during backpropagation training when existing capacity appears insufficient.
notes: Seed bibliography item verified against Crossref for the Connection Science article. Semantic Scholar also indexes a 1989 IJCNN version with DOI 10.1109/IJCNN.1989.118509. Automated review draft improved with Crossref API, DOI landing page, Semantic Scholar metadata, and targeted web search; still needs human full-text verification for the exact DNC trigger and training schedule. Synthesis note: post-growth stabilization is included as an open comparison axis because the automated review has not yet verified whether DNC freezes, continues, or otherwise constrains existing weights after insertion.

title: The Cascade-Correlation Learning Architecture
summary: Introduces a supervised constructive architecture that starts minimal, trains candidate units to correlate with residual error, installs the best unit, freezes it, and repeats.
growth_mechanism: Candidate hidden units compete by correlation with residual error; the best unit is installed and its incoming weights are frozen.
notes: Primary anchor paper for early site demos. Proceedings/Semantic Scholar index it under NeurIPS 1989, while this repository keeps the established 1990 ID pending a human bibliographic cleanup pass.

title: Constructive Learning of Recurrent Neural Networks: Limitations of Recurrent Cascade Correlation and a Simple Solution
summary: Analyzes recurrent cascade-correlation, proves topology-driven representational limitations for some finite-state automata, and sketches a constructive fully recurrent alternative that adds neurons during training.
growth_mechanism: Constructively adds neurons during recurrent-network training while preserving a fully recurrent structure, proposed as an alternative to recurrent cascade-correlation's restrictive topology.
notes: Metadata verified against IEEE Xplore and Penn State Pure pages during the 2026-06-24 weekly discovery dry run. The 2026-06-28 automated review improvement additionally checked Crossref and Semantic Scholar for DOI 10.1109/72.392247; the author-hosted PDF downloaded successfully, but local text extraction was not reliable enough for detailed full-text claims. The review draft is used here as a cautious synthesis bridge: it highlights that constructive growth rules can still impose restrictive topologies, especially in recurrent sequence-learning settings. Synthesis note: linked to post-growth stabilization for its caution that constructive recurrent growth must preserve enough recurrent topology, not merely add units.

title: Constructive Spiking Neural Networks for Simulations of Neuroplasticity
venue: PhD thesis, The University of Adelaide
summary: Develops a taxonomy for constructive neural networks and extends it into spiking simulations, proposing spike-timing-dependent construction and constructive algorithms for neuroplasticity-oriented simulations.
growth_mechanism: Treats growth as construction of neurons or synapses driven by constructive-algorithm processes; in the spiking branch these processes may depend on spike timing, local component performance, proxy-neuron events, or simulation expansion/contraction.
notes: Thesis source is public and maintained in a sibling repository. This web-book record points to a selective Chapter 2 taxonomy synthesis, not a verbatim thesis conversion. Includes a selective Stage 4 integration note on simulation expansion/contraction and plausible-effects constraints. Synthesis note: linked to post-growth stabilization through the thesis-derived plausible-effects constraint for simulation expansion/contraction.

title: Spike Timing Dependent Plasticity Finds the Start of Repeating Patterns in Continuous Spike Trains
summary: Shows that a single leaky integrate-and-fire neuron with STDP can become selective for the start of a repeating spatio-temporal spike pattern hidden in continuous distractor spike trains without an external time reference or firing-rate cue.
growth_mechanism: Does not add neurons directly; it provides a source-grounded STDP mechanism for selecting and strengthening early, predictive afferents, which this project treats as background for spike-timing-dependent construction and synapse-initialization themes.

title: Competitive Hebbian Learning Through Spike-Timing-Dependent Synaptic Plasticity
summary: Shows in modelling studies how spike-timing-dependent plasticity can make synapses compete for control of postsynaptic spike timing, strengthening short-latency or correlated inputs while weakening less effective ones.

title: What Can a Neuron Learn with Spike-Timing-Dependent Plasticity?
summary: Examines what transformations a single spiking neuron can learn under spike-timing-dependent plasticity with teacher forcing, contrasting lack of arbitrary-pattern convergence guarantees with positive average-case results for Poisson inputs under linear-separability-like conditions.
growth_mechanism: Does not propose structural growth; it frames the learnability limits and parameter-adaptation capabilities of STDP in a single spiking neuron, which constrains how much constructive spiking systems can expect from timing-dependent synapse initialization alone.
